**PayPal board rejects Stripe-Advent $53 billion bid as too low**

*PayPal's directors believe the joint offer undervalues the company and could face regulatory obstacles, keeping alive the largest potential deal in payments history.*

PayPal's board considers the $53 billion takeover approach from Stripe and Advent International inadequate, according to Reuters. Directors believe the offer undervalues the payments company and have flagged likely regulatory pushback as a further concern.

The bid, first reported on July 16, would represent the largest acquisition in the payments industry. A combined Stripe-PayPal entity would bring together two of the biggest online payment processors globally, raising immediate questions about market concentration in checkout and merchant acquiring. Stripe's core strength in developer-led commerce and PayPal's consumer wallet and branded checkout would overlap significantly in several segments.

PayPal has been restructuring under CEO Alex Chriss, who shut down the company's venture capital arm in June and has been narrowing focus on core payments and commerce. Whether the board's stance is a negotiating position or a firm rejection remains unclear, but the signal that $53 billion falls short sets a high bar for any revised approach.

*Sources: [PayPal board considers $53bn Stripe-Advent offer inadequate - Reuters](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48116/paypal-board-considers-53bn-stripe-advent-offer-inadequate---reuters?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**BBVA becomes first Spanish bank live on Swift's retail payments scheme**

*The launch extends Swift's new retail rulebook into Spain, adding momentum to an initiative designed to make cross-border payments for individuals and SMEs faster and more predictable.*

BBVA has gone live on Swift's new global retail payments scheme from its launch, becoming the first Spanish bank to join the initiative. The scheme establishes a common rulebook for international payments aimed at individuals and small businesses, with commitments around speed, transparency, predictability and round-the-clock availability.

Swift launched the retail scheme to bring cross-border payments closer to the experience users expect from domestic instant transfers. Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds and NatWest adopted the framework earlier this month, and BBVA's participation signals the scheme is gaining traction beyond its initial Anglo-Saxon base. Spain is a significant corridor for remittances and cross-border commerce, particularly with Latin America.

The scheme sits alongside other efforts to improve cross-border retail payments, such as the ECB's recent cross-currency instant payments pilot on TIPS and Citi's expansion of its correspondent banking instant payments network. For European banks, the question is how these overlapping initiatives coexist as each scales.

*Sources: [BBVA becomes first Spanish bank to launch Swift’s new global retail payments scheme](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110445/bbva-becomes-first-spanish-bank-to-launch-swifts-new-global-retail-payments-scheme?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**ACI Worldwide considers selling its billing division**

*A potential divestiture would narrow ACI's focus toward real-time payments infrastructure at a time when the company is processing instant payments for EPI and expanding through acquisitions such as Payment Components.*

ACI Worldwide is exploring a sale of its billing division, according to PYMNTS. The billing unit handles biller payment solutions, a business line that sits alongside ACI's core real-time payments processing and fraud prevention operations.

ACI was selected in June to process instant payments for the European Payments Initiative across Europe, and last year acquired Payment Components, a financial messaging and open banking solutions provider. Shedding the billing business would concentrate ACI's portfolio on the infrastructure layer for real-time and account-to-account payments, where demand is growing as SEPA instant payment mandates take effect and schemes such as Wero scale.

The move follows a broader pattern in payments infrastructure, where companies are narrowing their focus through selective divestitures. Pollen Street's carve-out of Finastra's Universal Banking business in June and Mastercard's reported consideration of selling Vocalink reflect similar portfolio discipline. Whether ACI finds a buyer at an acceptable price will depend on the billing unit's standalone economics, which remain undisclosed.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide Considers Putting Billing Division Up For Sale](https://www.pymnts.com/back-office/accounts-receivable/2026/aci-worldwide-considers-putting-billing-division-up-for-sale/) — PYMNTS.com*

**Euroclear appoints Usman Ahmad to lead digital assets strategy**

*Europe's largest securities settlement house has hired a dedicated digital assets head as tokenised securities move closer to production use across the continent's capital markets.*

Euroclear has appointed Usman Ahmad as head of digital assets. The role places Ahmad at the centre of the settlement infrastructure operator's efforts to position itself for tokenised securities, an area where European regulators and market participants are moving from proof-of-concept to pilot-stage work.

The appointment comes as tokenised real-world assets and distributed ledger technology gain regulatory attention across Europe. The BIS completed Project Aperta in June to prototype cross-border open finance interoperability, and Swift is preparing live transactions on its shared ledger with 17 banks. For Euroclear, which settles more than €1 trillion in securities transactions daily, the strategic question is whether tokenised instruments will flow through existing central securities depositories or bypass them entirely.

Whether this is a newly created position or a replacement is not stated in the source. Ahmad's background and previous role were not detailed in the available information.

*Sources: [Euroclear Appoints Usman Ahmad as Head of Digital Assets](https://fintechnews.ch/blockchain_bitcoin/euroclear-usman-ahmad-digital-assets/84735/) — Fintech News Switzerland*
